vehicles.slot: Pre-2016 XF: Emergency Park Release (EPR) lever hidden behind REAR of center console. Remove the narrow trim piece in front of the center storage compartment (no screws — pry gently with plastic tool). 2016+ XF: shift interlock override lever is in the ENGINE COMPARTMENT on the DRIVER-SIDE intake manifold — remove black plastic cover on intake manifold by lifting upward.
shift: PREFERRED (with power): Turn ignition to ON. Use JaguarDrive rotary selector — it rises from the console. Rotate to N.
WITHOUT POWER — Pre-2016 XF (EPR in console):
Remove the narrow trim piece at the REAR of the center console (in front of the storage compartment).
Use a flat-bladed screwdriver to rotate the locking device 90 degrees COUNTERCLOCKWISE.
Press the brake pedal firmly.
Pull the EPR lever UPWARD using the strap — pull until it latches in the vertical position.
The JaguarDrive selector will remain showing P, but the gear display will flash N — this is correct.
WITHOUT POWER — 2016+ XF (EPR under intake manifold):
Open the hood. Locate the driver-side intake manifold.
Remove the black plastic cover on the intake manifold by lifting upward.
Lift the black lever on the shift interlock override to the VERTICAL position.
Engage the securing latch to hold the lever in position.
Transmission stays in Neutral until the override is released.
neutral: Apply parking brake.
CRITICAL: The EPB (electronic parking brake) may also be engaged.
Activating the EPR releases the transmission Park lock — it may NOT automatically release the EPB.
If EPB remains engaged: in some cases connecting a jump pack and using the EPB service procedure may be needed.
For towing: confirm vehicle rolls freely before loading onto flatbed.
FLATBED preferred for all Jaguar XF models — AWD and FWD variants exist.
Battery is in the TRUNK on most XF generations. Jump terminals: some XF have a remote jump post under the hood.
Connect jump pack to battery in trunk, or use remote under-hood terminal if present.
vehicles.towMethod: RWD: lift from front (rear drive wheels roll). AWD: flatbed preferred.
towNotes: AWD system: flatbed safest.
Rotary dial requires power — jump first if dead.

epb.override: Restore 12V. Hold EPB button to release. Manual: remove EPB module connector in trunk and connect spade connectors to motor pins to retract.
steps: Manual fallback: EPB module in trunk right side. Disconnect connector, insert spade connectors into correct slots (Violet/Brown and Yellow/Green pins noted on 2009-2015 XF). Connect to 12V to retract.

battery.warnings: AGM battery. AWD: flatbed preferred. EPB manual release requires wiring connector access.

knownIssues.title: EPR Procedure Differs Between Pre-2016 and 2016+ XF
knownIssues.detail: Pre-2016 XF: EPR lever is behind the center console trim. 2016+ XF: shift interlock override is on the ENGINE COMPARTMENT driver-side intake manifold. Many operators and even some owners do not know the 2016+ location. Always confirm the model year before attempting console access.

knownIssues.title: EPR Does NOT Release the Electronic Parking Brake
knownIssues.detail: The EPR releases only the transmission Park lock. The Electronic Park Brake (EPB) is a separate system and may remain engaged. If the vehicle does not roll freely after activating EPR, the EPB is still applied. Restoring 12V power is required to release the EPB using the normal EPB service procedure.

vehicles.slot: Electronic touchscreen — Service menu for Tow Mode / Neutral. Override near selector base.
shift: I-Pace EV: FLATBED ONLY.
PREFERRED (with power): Touch the touchscreen to access the Service menu — put vehicle in Neutral/Tow mode.
WITHOUT POWER:
Attempt to restore 12V auxiliary power first — jump terminals under the hood (front).
Once powered, use touchscreen Service menu.
Emergency mechanical release: similar to XF EPR — remove rear console trim, rotate locking device, pull strap.
NEVER touch orange high-voltage cables or components.
neutral: FLATBED ONLY — electric drivetrain.
Connect jump pack to 12V auxiliary battery under the hood.
12V AUXILIARY ONLY — never touch HV battery.
Once powered, use touchscreen to select Neutral.
Emergency console EPR is a last resort (same procedure as XF).
vehicles.notes: FLATBED ONLY. Electric drivetrain. Tow Mode via touchscreen.
vehicles.warn: FLATBED ONLY. 12V only — never touch HV orange cables/battery.

epb.override: Restore 12V. Tow Mode on touchscreen releases EPB. Manual: EPB connector method (same as XF/F-Pace).
steps: Use Tow Mode on touchscreen — releases EPB and engages neutral.

battery.warnings: FLATBED ONLY. 12V auxiliary ONLY. Never touch orange HV cables.

knownIssues.title: FLATBED ONLY — Electric AWD
knownIssues.detail: The I-Pace has permanent AWD electric motors. Towing with any wheels on the ground will damage the drive units. Flatbed with Tow Mode active is the only safe method.

vehicles.slot: Emergency Park Release (EPR): remove rear center console trim piece (narrow piece in front of storage compartment — pry with plastic tool, no screws). Locking device and pull strap are behind this trim.
shift: PREFERRED (with power): Turn ignition to ON. JaguarDrive rotary selector rises. Rotate to N.
WITHOUT POWER — EPR procedure:
Remove the narrow trim piece at the REAR of the center console (no screws — pry gently).
Use a flat-bladed screwdriver to rotate the locking device 90 degrees COUNTERCLOCKWISE.
Press the brake pedal firmly.
Pull the EPR strap/lever UPWARD until it latches vertically.

Attempt to restore 12V power before EPR if possible (EPR works without power, but 12V helps confirm N).

Confirm vehicle rolls freely — EPB may still be engaged separately.

knownIssues.title: Aluminum Body — Do Not Hook or Chain
knownIssues.detail: The XJ uses an all-aluminum body structure. Standard chains or hooks on the body panels will cause serious damage. Always use wheel baskets/straps or hook only at proper tow points. Never drape chains over the body.

knownIssues.detail: The S-Type 12V battery is in the trunk (boot) on the passenger side. There is no battery under the hood. Always open the trunk to access jump terminals.
